metadata.name: turns-debate
metadata.description: Three advocates argue for a startup HQ city, one at a time; a chair watches the floor, scores every argument, and records the winner with a verdict.
metadata.author: bearpit

goals: Persuade the chair that your city is the best HQ: ${city_a,Austin,The city Ava argues for}, ${city_c,Miami,The city Mira argues for}, or ${city_b,Denver,The city Dan argues for}.
spec.guidelines:
This is a turn-based roundtable. When it is your turn you get ONE message to make your case for your assigned city — the system passes the floor after it, and you cannot post out of turn. Tool calls are free and never use up your turn: recall() your notes before you speak, and remember(...) afterwards what you mean to attack next round. Round 2 is for REBUTTAL — name a rival's claim and break it. After every advocate has spoken (a round or two), the chair scores each argument and records the winner with its verdict tool; that tool call, not anything said in chat, is what ends the debate.

EVIDENCE. You hold `web_fetch` and may read public pages. A claim you looked up and quoted outweighs one you asserted, so where a fact would settle a point — a cost, a tax rate, a population, a published ranking — go and get it, give the URL, and quote the words. Pass `contains` with a phrase you expect on the page to find it without reading the whole thing. Arguing from your own knowledge is legitimate; dressing it up as a source is not, and the chair holds the same tool.
